scale_0_100.label: Observability & Runtime Forensics

rubric.measurement: Inject one representative fault into each named product stage (overlay provider selection, message normalization, render and disconnect recovery). Count stages with a typed outcome, phase timing, and an explicit missing-source state. Compare against the same successful path at <=2% runtime overhead.

anchors.60: 40% of stages emit a typed outcome
anchors.70: 60% emit an outcome and phase timing
anchors.90: 100% expose outcomes in one external report.json
anchors.100: All also preserve fault attribution on failure, retry and an unavailable collector

rubric.falsifier: Compare each fault receipt with the successful path and check the external report independently.

levels.60: Basic stdout logs on errors; manual reproduction needed to locate stalls.
levels.70: Structured JSON/log events on main entrypoints and partial phase timing.

levels.90: report.json + per-stage p50/p95 timings + zero silent-catch paths + live failure counters feeding backlog.

scale_0_100.why_not_100: At 90 by the tier-90 anchor (report.json + per-stage timings + zero silent-catch paths), not 100: the 100 anchor needs correlated telemetry across every entrypoint, subprocess and I/O boundary with <2% overhead and instant root-cause attribution. The correlated boundary trace does not exist yet: `_tools/ko-census.mjs` counts silent exits at rest (guardShaped=4 of a 113 baseline) and `harness/twins/replay.mjs` replays a recorded ring, so a live fault is attributed by reading the ring chronology, not by following a request across boundaries.
